column1: # m0001 of PT/TT/CLNH/0086/11, pass B: one blind Sonnet subagent read of images/m0001_L01..L06.jpg only (no other file, no context beyond "c. 1800-1830 French hand, possibly a Portuguese word"), 2 Oct 2026. Copied verbatim from its report.

column2: Que Madame la Ctesse envoie toujours à B^a q[ue]...
column3: Que=H Madame=H la=H Ctesse=M envoie=M toujours=M à=H B^a=M q=M
column4: Ctesse is an abbreviation for Comtesse, written with a superscript. "envoie" could be "envoie" or "envoye". "toujours" is a slightly odd form, alternatives "toujoux" or "toujour". "B^a" with a superscript a, possibly Bª for Barbara or Bahia. The line is cut off at the right edge: it ends "q" or "g", probably "que" or "qu'".

column2: Son texte soit = venez - venez - venez = mais qu'elle
column3: Son=H texte=H soit=H venez=H venez=H venez=H mais=H qu'elle=M
column4: Dashes and '=' signs are as written. "texte" could be "teste". "soit" could be "soir". The final word is cut off at the right edge: "qu'elle" or "qu'ell[e]".

column2: ne ferme pas sa Lettre avant que de me voir ce
column3: ne=M ferme=H pas=H sa=H Lettre=H avant=H que=H de=H me=H voir=M ce=H
column4: Initial "ne" might be "ne" or "ni". "Lettre" has a capital L. "voir" could be "voir" or "voix". The line continues onto the next line at "soir".

column2: soir. J'ai travaillé, Dieu merci, comme un
column3: soir=H J'ai=H travaillé=H Dieu=H merci=H comme=H un=M
column4: soir is a line-start fragment with a full stop, continuing from L03 "ce soir". "un" could be "an" or "au". The full stop after "soir" is clear. The comma after "travaillé" is a bit unclear.

Cedilla on the c is clear. A full stop follows. Some faint ink marks lower right (a flourish at about x=550 and a mark near x=1010) may be bleed-through or the tops of letters from the next line, so not transcribed.

Reading uncertain. Alternatives for "Bráliz": "Brulyz", "Bruliz", "Bralyz", "Bráluz". "cui" could be "cuí", "aui" or "ceu". A raised colon-like mark follows (a colon or a stop). There is an accent over the "a". Probably Portuguese ("Brazil"-like or a place name). Not clear.

Large capital D with a looped flourish. "Desgostadíssimo" in Portuguese ("most displeased/vexed"). Alternatives for the middle letters: "Desgostadissimo" vs "Desgostadifsimo" (long s). The ending "-issimo" reads as "ifsimo" or "issimo" with a long s. A full stop follows. Probably a closing or signature line.

column1: # Language: mostly French (L01 to L05); L06 is Portuguese ("Desgostadissimo", and probably "Bráliz cui").
